summary: Recursive self-improvement began in the AGI and singularity literature of the early 2010s as the idea that an AI could repeatedly improve its own design, possibly triggering an intelligence explosion that raised safety and ethics worries. Today it mostly names a concrete, benchmarked engineering goal: LLM agents and AI research systems that turn feedback into lasting improvements to themselves, their harnesses, or the process of building AI.
